text: I'll start with the pod and the cluster capacity.

arguments.root_cause_statement: Deployment fraud/fraud-scoring asks for a CPU request of "512" in its pod template. In Kubernetes a bare number is whole CPU cores, so this is a request for 512 cores, almost certainly a typo for "512m" (half a core). The only node in the cluster, incident-lab-control-plane, has 6 allocatable CPU, so no node can ever satisfy the request. The scheduler rejects the pod with "0/1 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient cpu", pod fraud/fraud-scoring-596445859d-thcdh stays Pending with PodScheduled=False and no node assigned, so the Deployment reports ready=0/1 and no fraud scores are produced. Changing the request to "512m" makes the pod schedulable on the existing node.
arguments.mechanism: Deployment fraud/fraud-scoring sets .spec.template.spec.containers[scorer].resources.requests.cpu to "512", i.e. 512 whole cores rather than the intended "512m", while the only node incident-lab-control-plane has cpu=6/6 allocatable. The scheduler therefore fails to place the pod it creates and reports "0/1 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient cpu. preemption: 0/1 nodes are available: 1 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.", leaving pod fraud/fraud-scoring-596445859d-thcdh Pending with PodScheduled False and Node: none, so the Deployment stays at ready=0/1.

evidence.claim: The paged Deployment has no ready replicas and its only pod is Pending and unscheduled.
The pod is Pending with no node assigned.
The scheduler rejects the pod for insufficient CPU.
evidence.quote: 0/1 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient cpu. preemption: 0/1 nodes are available: 1 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.

evidence.claim: The only node in the cluster has 6 allocatable CPU, far less than the request.
The Deployment pod template itself carries the oversized cpu request that a human must edit.

ruled_out.alternative: The pod is blocked by node taints or a nodeSelector rather than by resources
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The pod has no node selector and only the default not-ready/unreachable tolerations, and the node reports Ready=True with no taints listed; the scheduler's own reason is Insufficient cpu, not a taint or selector mismatch.

ruled_out.alternative: A ResourceQuota or LimitRange in namespace fraud is blocking or rewriting the pod
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The namespace contains only a ConfigMap and a ServiceAccount besides the workload; no ResourceQuota or LimitRange exists, and the pod was admitted (it exists) and only failed at scheduling.

ruled_out.alternative: The container image or command is broken (ImagePullBackOff / CrashLoopBackOff)
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The pod never reached a node, so no container was ever created or pulled; its only condition is PodScheduled=False.
